## Install — no GitHub CLI, no tokens, no SSH keys

Download the **Source code (zip)** below, extract, and run the bundled installer. Same flow on every OS.

**macOS / Linux**
```bash
cd jtr-0.6.1
./install.sh
```

**Windows**
```powershell
cd .\jtr-0.6.1\
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1
```

The installer fetches `uv` if needed, then runs `uv tool install` on the extracted source. See [INSTALL.md](https://github.com/BD-AI-SDLC/jtr/blob/main/INSTALL.md) for manual steps and troubleshooting.

## What's new

Fixes `jtr auth sso` waiting out its full five-minute timeout after a login that had already succeeded, and stops it asking you to log in again on every run.

- **Fixed: SSO hung after a successful login.** The command decided it was authenticated only if a `fetch` issued from inside the browser page returned JSON. That is a proxy for the thing that actually matters — whether the browser's cookies authenticate a jtr request — and a fragile one: once the SSO chain left the tab on a raw REST response, the in-page fetch kept throwing and the command waited out its timeout while the cookies in that same browser were already good. It now checks the cookies directly on every poll, using the same verification the rest of jtr uses. A login that has worked is detected immediately.
- **Your login is remembered between runs.** The browser profile is kept at `~/.jtr/browser-profile` instead of being discarded, so the identity provider can skip the login form on subsequent runs. Previously every `jtr auth sso` started from a blank browser and made you sign in from scratch, even if you had just done so.
- **`jtr auth logout` clears that profile too**, so logging out still logs you out rather than leaving a session the next `jtr auth sso` would silently reuse.
- **Better diagnostics.** A failed in-page probe used to report a bare `status=0` and throw away the reason. The error text is now included in the progress line.

## Upgrading

Install as usual. No config, cookie, or `.env` changes.

The new `~/.jtr/browser-profile` directory (mode 0700) holds a browser session on disk, alongside the cookie file that already lives there. Delete it, or run `jtr auth logout`, to be prompted for a fresh login.

## Assets
- `install.sh` — macOS / Linux installer
- `install.ps1` — Windows installer
- `jtr-0.6.1-py3-none-any.whl`, `jtr-0.6.1.tar.gz` — build artifacts (auto-detected by the installers if placed alongside them)
